requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate succeeded against a loop-backed PV (/dev/loop9), mkfs.xfs formatted it, and it was mounted at /srv/data (997M, 4% used). fstab and a systemd oneshot unit were added so the mount is reproducible, and post-restart evidence confirms the mount persists.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2GB while it stays mounted and contents remain intact
requirements.summary: Baseline files (3x50MB + marker) with sha256 checksums were written before growth. lvextend -L 2200M and xfs_growfs were run while the filesystem stayed mounted; df confirmed 2.2G size, and sha256sum -c confirmed all checksums matched post-growth, directly demonstrating no data loss during the online resize.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — an LV mounted at /srv/data and grown to ≥2GB while remaining mounted with contents intact — are directly and coherently evidenced via checksum verification before and after the online resize. The executor also independently ran the full node-restart evidence protocol: a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 809708f3...) was captured, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node came back with a different boot_id (4c2d4848...) matching the fixed lifecycle snapshot cross-check, and post-restart state showed the loop device reattached, VG/LV active, the filesystem mounted at 2.2G, and all file checksums intact — a complete, satisfied restart/recovery transition even though persistence was not explicitly required by the task.
limitations: Package-manager consistency check was unavailable (timed out) in both before/after global snapshots, so package-state hygiene beyond the observed yum/repo actions could not be independently cross-checked.

The necessity of the temporary CentOS-vault repo addition is somewhat ambiguous since a concurrent background yum process appears to have installed lvm2 independently; this is noted as a minor hygiene caveat, not a task failure, since the repo file was fully removed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were largely read-only discovery or directly purposeful (PV/VG/LV creation, formatting, mounting, growing, checksum verification, persistence wiring, restart verification). One borderline mutation: a temporary CentOS-vault yum repo file was added (cmd-4220c36c71b24dde) to install lvm2 after finding subscription-manager repos disabled; by the time it finished (after a long yum-lock wait), lvm2 was already installed by a separate background process (cmd-518f65ae175b4094 shows 'already installed'), suggesting the repo addition may not have been strictly necessary — but it was bounded, low-risk (gpgcheck=0 vault repo used only briefly), and fully removed afterward (cmd-4c775db89d1c4715) with no residue. The loop-file-backed LVM workaround (since vda had no free space) is a reasonable, non-destructive design choice given the constrained disk layout, not a hygiene issue. Package-health checks were unavailable (timeout) in both before/after snapshots, which is an environment limitation, not executor-caused.
